papers.title: A high current anodization to fabricate a nano-porous structure on the surface of Ti-based implants.
papers.abstract: In this study, an oxide layer on Ti-based implants is fabricated by using a high current anodization (HCA) technique in the nitrate electrolyte. This layer is composed of micro-pits and nano-porous arrays in the honeycomb structure. The results show that both the roughness and the layer thickness are related to the reaction time, whereas the size of nano-pores has little to do with the anodization duration. Compared to the nano-tubular arrays constructed by the conventional anodization, this nano-porous layer shows significantly improved mechanical stability. Furthermore, the in vitro assay of osteoblasts shows that cells behaviors on this surface can be modulated by the topology of this special layer. A suitable hierarchical structure composed of micro-pits and nano-porous structure can significantly stimulate osteoblasts attachment, activity, spreading and ALP function. Therefore, this hierarchical surface layer may provide a promising approach, which endows the Ti-based implants with better stability and osseointegration.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及钛基植入体的阳极氧化表面改性，与增材制造生物材料方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not involve additive manufacturing (LPBF/AM), no mechanical testing, and no stress shielding analysis.

summary_zh.motivation: 通过高电流阳极氧化在钛植入体表面构建纳米多孔结构以改善骨整合。
summary_zh.method: 使用硝酸电解液进行高电流阳极氧化，形成微坑和纳米多孔阵列。
summary_zh.result: 纳米多孔层显著提高了机械稳定性，并促进了成骨细胞附着和功能。
summary_zh.validation: 通过体外成骨细胞实验验证表面拓扑对细胞行为的影响。

summary_en.motivation: To fabricate a nano-porous oxide layer on Ti-based implants via high current anodization for enhanced osseointegration.
summary_en.method: High current anodization in nitrate electrolyte produces a hierarchical surface with micro-pits and nano-porous arrays.
summary_en.result: The nano-porous layer exhibits improved mechanical stability compared to conventional nano-tubular layers and stimulates osteoblast attachment and function.
summary_en.validation: In vitro osteoblast assays confirm that cell behavior is modulated by the surface topology.
